title: The Ocean
materials: Household rhythm sticks or wooden spoons
quest_mission: Join Vesta & Silas in Terrasol on an acoustic sensory quest to explore The Ocean.
rhythm_ignition: Teacher models a steady 2-minute rhythmic call-and-response beat to 'The Ocean', synchronizing clapping and vocal chanting with the children.
tactile_ritual:
The Hands-On Sensory Discovery:
1. Children gather in a circle with tactile items.
2. Follow the musical cues of The Ocean to touch, sort, and move in rhythmic unison.
3. Pair high-reach movements with deep somatic exhalations.
4. Freeze in quiet stillness at the final chord.

socratic_wonder_circle.rhythm_cue: 60 BPM Slow Ocean-Wave Exhale (Listen Deeply Before Speaking)
socratic_wonder_circle.wait_time_rule: Hold a calm 4-beat pause after every question before inviting responses.
prompts: Evaluating Evidence (S-33): As we listen to slow 60 BPM ocean waves, what do you notice happening to the speed of your own breathing and shoulders?
Evaluating Explanations (S-18): When we ripple a water tray or jump rope, why do waves look like the water is racing forward even though a floating cork mostly bobs up and down?
Intellectual Humility (S-5): Much of the deep ocean has never been seen by human eyes—why does admitting 'We don't know yet' make ocean explorers better scientists?

age_tier_scaffolds.Sprouts (Ages 2–4): Sway softly with 60 BPM wave breaths and tap gentle crest-up, trough-down motions.
age_tier_scaffolds.Pathfinders (Ages 4–5): Watch a floating leaf or cork on rippled water and describe what it actually does.
age_tier_scaffolds.Wayfarers (Ages 6–7): Connect ocean waves (water energy) with acoustic sound waves (air vibration) using direct observation.

remodelled_unit_refs: Unit #64: Parts of a Wave (PDF p.276)

domain_spider.language: Articulate clear auditory phrasing and target vocabulary connected to The Ocean.
domain_spider.cognitive: Identify rhythmic patterns, tempo shifts, and conceptual categories in Terrasol.
domain_spider.physical: Gross motor whole-body balance, bilateral coordination, and fine motor finger rhythm.
domain_spider.science_sensory: Tactile exploration of real-world materials and acoustic auditory pitch discrimination.
domain_spider.social_emotional: Cooperative participation, shared attentional focus, and calming self-regulation.

teacher_whisper: Auditory rhythmic pacing stimulates brainstem regulation and synchronizes attention across the classroom without visual screen fatigue.

standards.kindergarten_readiness: Actively participates in screen-free multi-sensory rhythm rituals and articulates key conceptual observations.
